newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates close lower on NCD maturity.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates close lower on NCD maturity.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed lower on Thursday as maturity of T$8 billion worth of negotiable certificates of deposit fuelled liquidity in the banking system, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate finished at 5.735 percent against Wednesday's 5.983 close, with 30-day commercial paper at 5.60-5.75 percent against 6.00.
The central bank had issued NCDs repeatedly in the past week to mop up excessive funds, but it refrained from doing so on Wednesday amid sharp rate upswings.
The banking system's daily reserve excess on Wednesday returned to a postive T$3.5 billion from recent negative figures after the central bank stopped issuing NCDs.
The government bond yields fell on Thursday on strengthened buying as money rates dropped and the stock index closed below a psychological support at 8,000 points, dealers said.
On Thursday the stock index ended 60.81 points or 0.75 percent lower at 7,997.65.
The benchmark 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 5.850 percent against Wednesday's 5.900-902 close.
